label: bm-resin-water-uptake-data
topic: Measured water uptake and hygroscopic swelling of acrylate photopolymers
summary: I found no measured linear hygroscopic strain, hygroscopic expansion coefficient or water diffusivity for any Formlabs resin in any independent paper, so that gap in the project record stands. What I found instead changes two earlier claims. (1) The earlier statement that every current Formlabs SLA resin gains under 1 percent mass in water is wrong for Flexible 80A Resin V2: its own 2026 data sheet (ASTM D471 slab, deionized water) reports +8 percent mass and +3 percent volume after 1 day and +9 percent mass and +7 percent volume after 1 week. The 0.7 percent figure in the earlier chemistry file is the Formlabs solvent-page row labelled plain 'Flexible 80A Resin' (the older V1, 1 cm cube, 24 h); both numbers are real, they describe different resin versions and test methods. My arithmetic turns the V2 volume figures into an isotropic linear strain of about 0.99 percent (1 day) and 2.28 percent (1 week), i.e. 0.124 and 0.253 percent strain per percent mass gain; this is the largest measured water response of a stock Formlabs resin and, with Rigid 10K (<0.1 percent) as passive layer, would give a bilayer curvature radius of about 54 mm (1 day) and 23 mm (1 week) at h = 0.8 mm using kappa = 1.5*d_eps/h. (2) Elastic 50A V1 is the only Formlabs sheet that prints both size and weight gain: in solvents the linear strain per percent mass gain is 0.44 to 0.52 (ideal volume mixing would give about 0.40 for water); for water it prints weight +2.3 percent and size '<1 percent', so only an upper bound of 0.435 per percent mass is measured. The independent literature gives sorption, not strain, for Formlabs: Denture Base OP 17.86 ug/mm3 at 48 h (Gad 2022) versus 7.53 ug/mm3 at 7 d (Izzettinoglu 2025), a 2.4-fold disagreement I cannot explain, and a Form 3 Clear Resin tetrahedron that lost 0.29 percent mass on baking with no length change within +-0.15 mm on 48 mm (Radic 2024). Water diffusivity in printed methacrylate photopolymer is about 1e-12 m2/s (0.85e-12 reported for a DLP-printed resin; my recheck of the same paper's medians gives about 2.6e-13; UDMA resin 6.9e-12 in a cast dental study), so a 0.4 mm layer needs roughly 2 to 7 days to equilibrate. Paired mass-and-strain data exist only for filled dental composites (0.68 to 2.83 percent mass with 0.74 to 4.79 percent expansion, which I read as volumetric, about 0.36 to 0.56 percent linear per percent mass) and for solvents in Elastic 50A V1; for printed neat resins in water I found none.
lay_summary: Most plastic resins that Formlabs printers use hardly soak up water, so a printed strip would barely change shape in humid air. One soft resin, Flexible 80A Version 2, is different: Formlabs' own test says a slab gains 8 percent of its weight in water in a day. Think of a dry sponge, but a very stiff and slow one. That much water makes it grow about 1 percent in length in a day and 2 percent in a week, which is enough to curl a thin two-layer strip if the other layer stays dry. No independent lab has measured how much a Formlabs resin grows when it soaks up water, so the team would have to measure it. Water also moves into these plastics slowly, taking days rather than minutes to fill a layer half a millimetre thick.

glossary.plain: A liquid that turns solid when light shines on it; what resin 3D printers use.
How much water a material soaks up, usually as a percentage of its dry weight.
The growth in size of a material as it takes in water or moist air.
How much longer something gets, as a fraction of its original length (1 percent means 1 mm per 100 mm).
Swelling the same amount in every direction, so a volume change can be turned into a length change by taking a cube root.
A number that says how fast water creeps into a material; small numbers mean slow.
Two glued layers where one swells and one does not, so the strip bends like a bimetal thermostat.
Standard test recipes for soaking plastics or rubber in a liquid and measuring weight or size change.
Micrograms of water taken up per cubic millimetre of material; dentists use it instead of a percentage.
The assumption that the water simply adds its own volume to the plastic, with no empty gaps.

findings.claim: Flexible 80A Resin V2 (current Formlabs elastomer): deionized water gives +8% mass and +3% volume after 1 day (hardness -26 Shore A points) and +9% mass and +7% volume after 1 week, by ASTM D471 on rectangular slabs wiped dry and weighed at once. Slab thickness is not stated in the data sheet. Row order reconstructed from PDF word coordinates because the extracted text is scrambled.
findings.value: 1 d: +8% mass, +3% vol; 1 wk: +9% mass, +7% vol
findings.confidence: high (mass, volume); medium that the row/label pairing is right
findings.evidence_quote: Deionized Water 1 day -26 +8% +3% 94% 89% ; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88% (Rectangular slabs ... evaluated immediately after wiping dry without a conditioning period.)

findings.claim: Own arithmetic: converting the V2 volume changes to isotropic linear strain gives 0.99% (1 day) and 2.28% (1 week), i.e. 0.124 and 0.253 percent strain per percent mass gain. Calculation: 1.03^(1/3)-1 = 0.00990; 0.00990/8 = 0.00124 per mass-percent; 1.07^(1/3)-1 = 0.02281; 0.02281/9 = 0.00253. Isotropy is assumed.

Own check on the V2 table: volume gain divided by the volume that ideal mixing would give (mass gain x 1.09/1.00) is 0.34 at 1 day (3 vs 8.72) and 0.71 at 1 week (7 vs 9.81). So at 1 day the water mass exceeds the swelling by about 3x; by 1 week the ratio is near the 0.54-0.73 efficiency the earlier chemistry file took from polyamide 6.6. The same table's solvent volumes are 1.8x (IPA 45% mass, 113% volume) to 2.0x (acetone) larger than ideal mixing, which suggests the D471 volume column is not a clean additive measurement; treat the 3% and 7% volume values with caution.
findings.source: own calculation, calc.py; solvent densities 0.785 and 0.79 g/cm3 are unverified background

findings.claim: CONTRADICTS spec-resin-chemistry.json (finding 'Every current Formlabs SLA resin gains under 1% mass in water at 24 h' and the summary line 'Flexible 80A 0.7%'): the Formlabs solvent-compatibility page row 'Flexible 80A Resin' does give water 0.7 (1 cm cube, 24 h), but that row belongs to the older Flexible 80A (acetone 37.4, IPA 11.7, xylene 64.1) and the current V2 data sheet reports +8% mass in 1 day by a different method (D471 slab). Different resin version and different method; both numbers are correctly transcribed. The earlier file's blanket statement fails for V2. CONFIRMS spec-formlabs-materials.json on the +8%/+3%/+9%/+7% values.
findings.source: https://formlabs.com/support/solvent-compatibility/ (saved solvent_compat2.html, table row 'Flexible 80A Resin') and the V2 TDS above
findings.confidence: high for the numbers; medium for the explanation (I did not find a page stating the row is V1)
findings.evidence_quote: Formlabs measures resistance to solvents by observing, measuring, and weighing printed cubes (originally measuring 1 cm × 1 cm × 1 cm) before and after immersion in a solvent for 24 hours.

findings.claim: Same Formlabs solvent page, water column (weight gain after 24 h, 1 cm cube): Elastic 50A V1 2.3; Elastic 50A V2 0.7; BioMed Elastic 50A 0.7; BioMed Flex 80A 0.6; TPU 90A 0.9; Clear V5 0.9; Grey V5 0.8; Tough 2000 V2 0.19; Tough 1500 V2 0.21; Rigid 4000 0.7; ESD 0.7; Rigid 10K <0.1; Silicone 40A <0.1; Tough 1000 0.0. This reproduces the earlier files.
findings.evidence_quote: Results are reported as weight gain percentage after 24 hours of exposure to solvent.

findings.claim: CONFIRMS the earlier '39 percent isopropanol' claim for Elastic 50A V2 (IPA 39.2) and Rigid 10K (IPA <0.1); the V1 Elastic 50A takes up 25.6 percent IPA on the same page and in its own data sheet, so the figure is version-specific.

Elastic 50A V1 data sheet (Spanish copy, 24 h, printed post-cured 1x1x1 cm cube) prints size gain AND weight gain: water size <1 %, weight 2.3 %. Only an upper bound on strain per mass gain follows: <1/2.3 = <0.435 % per mass-%. Sea water 3.5% NaCl: size <1, weight 1.7.
findings.source: https://digilab.uma.es/pdf/form-3bl/Fichas-tecnicas-resinas/Ficha-tecnica-Elastic-50A.pdf page 2 (rows aligned by y coordinate); saved elastic50a_v1_tds.pdf
findings.confidence: high for weight; the size figure is only a '<1' threshold
findings.evidence_quote: Incremento de tamaño en 24 h (%) | Incremento de peso en 24 h (%) ... Agua <1 2,3

findings.claim: First measured coefficient in the Formlabs record, from solvents in the same Elastic 50A V1 sheet: linear size gain over weight gain = 19.3/37.3 = 0.517 (acetone), 13.3/25.6 = 0.520 (IPA), 18.2/39.6 = 0.460 (butyl acetate), 20.4/46.6 = 0.438 (xylene), 9.9/21.7 = 0.456 (Skydrol 5), percent strain per percent mass. This is consistent with ideal volume mixing at a resin density near 1.2 g/cm3 (implied 1.13 to 1.23, using unverified background solvent densities). For water, ideal mixing predicts 1.2/3 = 0.40 per mass-% or 0.92 % strain at 2.3 % mass, which agrees with the printed '<1 %'.
findings.value: 0.44 to 0.52 %-strain per mass-% in solvents; ~0.40 predicted for water
findings.source: own calculation, calc.py (elastic50a_v1_solvent_coefficients) from the V1 data sheet

findings.claim: Independent Form 3 data point: Formlabs Clear Resin tetrahedra (48 mm sides, printed by an outside service on a Form 3) lost 0.29 +- 0.005 % of 17.27 g on a 48 h vacuum bake at up to 120 C, and side lengths stayed 4.80 cm within the +-0.15 mm manufacturing tolerance. No length change was resolved. Upper bound on strain per mass-% is 0.15/48 x 100/0.29 = 1.08, too weak to be useful. The authors argue re-uptake is a surface effect over under 2 weeks at 21.5 C and 32.7 %RH, and estimate maximum water content about 1.6 % from literature PMMA/HPMA values (an estimate, not a measurement).
findings.value: 0.29 % mass loss; length unchanged within 0.15 mm / 48 mm (0.31 %)
findings.evidence_quote: The mean mass lost during baking was 0.29 ± 0.005 % from the initial 17.27 ± 0.05 g mean.

findings.claim: Independent measurement on a Formlabs resin: Denture Base OP (Form 3+), 50 x 0.5 mm discs, distilled water 48 h at 37 C, ISO 20795 method: water sorption 17.86 (SD 0.83) ug/mm3 before and 25.92 (SD 1.2) after 5000 thermal cycles, lowest of the three printed resins tested (NextDent 19.83, Asiga 20.1) and above heat-cured acrylic (16.1). At an assumed density of 1.20 g/cm3 this is 1.49 % and 2.16 % by mass.
findings.confidence: high for the table; medium for the mass-% conversion (density assumed)

findings.claim: A second independent paper on the same Formlabs Denture Base OP resin (Form 3, 50 um layers, Form Cure 80 C, discs 15 x 2 mm, distilled water 7 days) reports sorption of only 7.53 +- 1.74 ug/mm3 (air cure) and 8.12 +- 1.95 (glycerin cure) after 7 days, about 0.63 and 0.68 % at 1.20 g/cm3. That is 2.4x LOWER than Gad 2022 at 48 h, although immersion was longer. The two papers disagree and I cannot explain it (thickness 0.5 vs 2 mm, drying protocol, and the second paper's negative solubility of about -8 ug/mm3 are all candidates; unverified).

Dental LT Clear (Formlabs) was tested in an independent 28-day artificial-saliva study (14 mm x 2 mm discs, 37 C) but printed on a SprintRay Pro 95 DLP printer, not a Formlabs printer; the water-absorption percentages are only in Figure 2 and I could not read them. The paper states water uptake was significantly higher than conventional PMMA and that nanoindentation hardness and modulus fell significantly with immersion time.
findings.evidence_quote: The hardness and elastic modulus values of both 3D-printed materials (obtained using the nanoindentation test) decreased significantly as the immersion period rose

findings.claim: Independent paper with Dental LT Clear V2 sorption and solubility (ISO 4049, 15 mm discs, distilled water 37 C, 7 days) exists, but the values are in a table image/link I could not read; the extracted text only says coating changed solubility, not sorption. A Duran sorption of '11.835 %' in the same text looks like a unit slip against ug/mm3 and I did not use it.
findings.evidence_quote: Coating significantly decreased water solubility for Dental LT, but no change was seen in water sorption.

findings.claim: DLP-printed (Asiga UV Max, 385 nm) methacrylate PMMA-type resin plates, 10 x 10 x 1 mm, distilled water 37 C: median sorption 11.1 ug/mm3 at 24 h rising to 39.8 at 14 days (resin IV; others 9.7 to 11.6 at 24 h and 37.0 to 39.5 at 14 d), with no plateau by 14 days. At 1.20 g/cm3 assumed that is 0.93 % at 24 h and 3.3 % at 14 d. Printed material showed a biphasic curve with a sharp rise after 72 h and ended above the milled PMMA (28.3). The 24 h value agrees with Formlabs' under-1 % cube figures; the 14 d value shows that 24 h tests understate uptake by about 3.5x.
findings.value: 0.93 % (24 h) to 3.3 % (14 d, still rising), density assumed
findings.confidence: high for medians; medium for % conversion

findings.claim: Reported diffusion coefficient in that paper: 1.02-1.15e-12 m2/s for milled and 0.85e-12 m2/s for printed PMMA-type material (D = 0.049 L^2/t_half, L = 1 mm). My recheck from the paper's own medians: milled t_half about 14 h gives D = 9.6e-13 (agrees); printed material has not reached half of its 14 d value until about 53 h, so D is about 2.6e-13, three times lower than reported (the reported value implies t_half = 16 h). The printed curve is biphasic, so a single Fickian D is nominal.
findings.evidence_quote: Diffusion coefficient was calculated and values as D = 1.02–1.15 × 10 −12 m 2 /s for milled and 0.85 × 10 −12 m 2 /s for printed materials were obtained.

findings.claim: Cast light-cured dental dimethacrylate neat resins, 37 C: water diffusion coefficients Bis-GMA 11.01e-8, Bis-EMA 7.43e-8, UDMA 6.88e-8, D3MA 6.22e-8, TEGDMA 1.52e-8 cm2/s, i.e. 1.1e-11, 7.4e-12, 6.9e-12, 6.2e-12, 1.5e-12 m2/s (unit conversion 1 cm2 = 1e-4 m2). The abstract does not say which liquid the quoted maxima belong to; it says D is higher in water than in ethanol mixtures. Urethane dimethacrylate (UDMA) is the nearest neat-resin analogue of urethane acrylates.
findings.evidence_quote: Bis-GMA-resin showed the highest diffusion coefficient (11.01 × 10⁻⁸cm² s⁻¹) followed by Bis-EMA-resin (7.43 × 10⁻⁸ cm² s⁻¹), UDMA-resin (6.88 × 10⁻⁸ cm² s⁻¹)

findings.claim: Same lab, same resins: the volume increase after water or ethanol sorption depends linearly on the amount absorbed (discs 15 mm x 1 mm, 30 days, 37 C, Archimedes volume). The slope values are in the full text, which I could not read, so no coefficient can be computed from it.
findings.evidence_quote: The volume increase was found to depend linearly on the amount of water or ethanol absorbed.

findings.claim: Filled dental composites, 15 x 2 mm discs, distilled water 37 C, 150 days, laser-micrometer diameter: mass change 0.68 % (+-0.02) for Filtek Silorane to 2.83 % (+-0.11) for Vertise Flow, with hygroscopic expansion 0.74 % (+-0.05) to 4.79 % (+-0.18). The abstract does not say whether expansion is linear or volumetric. If 4.79 % were linear the volume gain would be 15.1 % for 2.83 % mass, impossible for water addition, so I read it as volumetric: linear equivalents 0.25 % and 1.57 %, i.e. 0.36 and 0.56 percent linear per percent mass. As reported the ratio is 1.09 and 1.69. The authors also say the relation is non-linear at first.
findings.value: 0.36 to 0.56 % linear strain per mass-% (reading as volumetric)
findings.source: DOI 10.1016/j.dental.2013.05.010 via Europe PMC abstract; own calculation calc.py (wei2013_composites)
findings.confidence: medium-low (abstract only; linear vs volumetric inferred)
findings.evidence_quote: Mass changes after 150 d water immersion ranged from 0.68% (±0.02) for FS to 2.83% (±0.11) for VF and the corresponding hygroscopic expansions were from 0.74% (±0.05) for FS to 4.79% (±0.18) for VF.

findings.claim: Same group on eight composites (15 x 2 mm, 37 C, 150 d): volumetric hygroscopic expansion ranged 0.58 to 2.26 and equilibrium was reached by 60 days at 2 mm thickness. Value check for time scale: a 2 mm composite disc equilibrates in about 2 months.
findings.evidence_quote: The volumetric hygroscopic expansion ranged from 0.58 to 2.26 and can be considered in three bands.

findings.claim: UV-cured polyurethane acrylate (urethane acrylate): Tey et al. measured a coefficient of moisture expansion (CME) and report it about 35 % lower than the coefficient of ink expansion for fully cured material, and that swelling per unit solvent uptake rises with degree of cure. The numeric CME values are in the paywalled full text; I could not read them.
findings.evidence_quote: the coefficient of moisture expansion (CME) was found to be ∼ 35% lower than the coefficient of ink expansion (CIE) for a fully cured PUA

findings.claim: Low-cost LCD-printer acrylates (Elegoo Mars 3), 60 x 60 x 1 mm, 23 C distilled water, immersion to constant mass: saturation uptake Esun standard 5.02 %, Elegoo ABS-like 4.06 %, Conjure JAMG HE Tough 17.44 % (seawater 4.30, 3.41, 13.49). Time: HE Tough 12.37 % at 2.5 d of 13.49 %, ABS-like stable within 4 d, Esun not saturated until after 8 d. My crude Fickian D from those times: 1.07e-12, about 1.1e-12 and about 5.4e-13 m2/s (assumes Fickian, 98 % of saturation at the stated time). No dimensional change was measured (visual check only).
findings.value: 4 to 17 % mass at saturation; D about 5e-13 to 1.1e-12 m2/s
findings.confidence: high for uptake; low-medium for D

findings.claim: Bis-EMA / urethane-acrylate oligomer SLA resins, 10 mm x 1.5 mm films, water 25 C for 7 days: sorption 15.1 to 16.5 ug/mm3 (about 1.3 to 1.4 % at assumed 1.20 g/cm3), solubility 2.9 to 3.6 ug/mm3. Highest uptake is the blend with most oligomer and TMPTMA (B2T1O7). No dimensions.
findings.evidence_quote: B100 1.52 15.1 2.9 ... B2T1O7 1.53 16.5 3.6 (Water Absorption (µg/mm 3 ) Water Solubility (µg/mm 3 ))

findings.claim: Printed PEG-acrylate resins (Asiga PICO2 DLP, 385 nm, discs 9 mm x 1 mm, PBS 24 h) swell by DIAMETER 3.5 % (RC1) to 19.3 % (RC4) and 74.1 % (RC5, PEGMEMA-based), TPGDA-based under 0.5 %. CONFIRMS the earlier chemistry file. Mass was not reported, so no strain-per-mass coefficient can be computed from this paper.
findings.evidence_quote: TPGDA-based resins showed the lowest swelling ratio with less than 0.5% over a period of 24 h in PBS.

findings.claim: Filled dental composites (Z250, TPH, Flow), 10 mm x 2 mm discs, water 37 C, optical-microscope linear expansion: Z250 0.52 % (day 1) to 0.71 % (day 30), TPH 0.5 to 0.66, Flow 0.07 to 0.45, stabilising from about day 7. Mass was not reported, so no coefficient. The authors' own volumetric values (1.98, 1.35, 2.13 %) disagree with literature values they cite and they blame uncontrolled temperature and low microscope precision; I rate this paper low quality.

PolyJet rigid acrylate photopolymers (Stratasys materials data sheet, ASTM D570-98 24 h): VeroClear RGD810 1.1-1.5 %, RGD720 1.5-2.2 %, Digital ABS/RGD525 family 1.2-1.4 % (page 1, column assignment from the header order); Vero/Durus opaque grades 1.1-1.5 to 1.5-2.2 %; the rubber-like Tango and Agilus30 pages print no water-absorption line.
findings.source: https://pocc-techpark.media.uconn.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/2880/2020/10/MSS_PJ_PJMaterialsDataSheet-1-1.pdf (a copy of a Stratasys sheet dated 2017); saved stratasys_pj_matsheet.pdf
findings.confidence: medium (copy of a vendor sheet, column assignment by header order)
findings.evidence_quote: Water Absorption D-570-98 24hr % 1.5-2.2 % 1.5-2.2 Water Absorption D-570-98 24hr % 1.1-1.5 % 1.1-1.5

findings.claim: Carbon RPU 70 (dual-cure rigid polyurethane/methacrylate, DLS): water absorption under 0.5 % at 24 h and under 1.5 % at 14 days (ASTM D570). Carbon EPU 41 green parts: distilled water gives under 5 % mass gain after one week (ASTM D543 bin '<5 %'), and the sheet adds that values do not represent dimensional change. Urethane elastomer EPU 41 therefore takes up to a few percent of water at most, with no strain data.
findings.confidence: medium (RPU values assigned by row order in a scrambled table); high for EPU 41 bin
findings.evidence_quote: Distilled Water < 5% ... *Percent weight gained after one week submersion following ASTM D543. Values do not represent changes in dimension or mechanical properties.

findings.claim: Water-based design implication, own arithmetic with the project-record law kappa = 1.5*d_eps/h at optimal thickness ratio and radius R = h/(1.5*d_eps): for a Flexible 80A V2 active layer against a passive layer of about zero swelling (Rigid 10K, <0.1 % mass), h = 0.8 mm, d_eps = 0.99 % gives R = 0.8/(1.5 x 0.0099) = 53.9 mm at 1 day of immersion and d_eps = 2.28 % gives R = 23.4 mm at 1 week. This uses immersion data (not humid air) and assumes isotropic swelling.
findings.value: R about 54 mm (1 d), about 23 mm (1 wk) at h = 0.8 mm
findings.source: own calculation (project-record bilayer law; inputs from the V2 TDS)

findings.claim: Time to equilibrium implied by the diffusivities (t = L^2/D): D = 0.85e-12 gives 52 h at 0.4 mm and 327 h at 1.0 mm; D = 2.6e-13 gives 171 h and 1068 h; UDMA resin D = 6.88e-12 gives 6.5 h and 40 h. A 0.4 mm layer of printed methacrylate therefore needs days, matching the 14 d no-plateau curve above.

Water diffusion in photocured aliphatic poly(urethane acrylate) films was measured spectroscopically by Krongauz and Chawla; the abstract prints the coefficient as 'ranged from 5x 10.11 /sec', garbled (probably 5e-11 in unknown units), so I do not use it.

No hygroscopic expansion coefficient (strain per %RH or per mass-%), no moisture isotherm and no diffusivity for any Formlabs resin was found in any independent paper in this run. Searches covered dental, microfluidic, vacuum and soft-robotics literature plus Crossref and Europe PMC open-access queries. The only dimensional data on a Formlabs part are the Radic null result and Formlabs' own '<1 %' size column. This confirms the earlier files' gap and does not close it.
findings.source: search record in this report; see could_not_find

key_claims.claim: Flexible 80A Resin V2 gains +8 % mass and +3 % volume after 1 day and +9 % mass and +7 % volume after 1 week in deionized water (ASTM D471 slab), unlike the under-1 % cube figures for other Formlabs resins.
Elastic 50A V1 prints both size and weight change for a 24 h cube: in solvents size/weight is 0.44 to 0.52, and in water weight is +2.3 % with size only '<1 %'.
key_claims.evidence_quote: Incremento de tamaño en 24 h (%) | Incremento de peso en 24 h (%) ... Agua <1 2,3

key_claims.claim: No independent measurement of linear hygroscopic strain exists for a Formlabs resin; the nearest independent data are sorption values for Denture Base OP that disagree 2.4-fold (17.86 ug/mm3 at 48 h vs 7.53 at 7 d) and a Form 3 Clear Resin null length result.

Water diffusivity in printed methacrylate photopolymer is of order 1e-12 m2/s or lower (0.85e-12 reported; about 2.6e-13 on my recheck), with sorption still rising at 14 days (11.1 to 39.8 ug/mm3), so layers of 0.4 mm and up need days to equilibrate.
key_claims.evidence_quote: Diffusion coefficient was calculated and values as D = 1.02–1.15 × 10 −12 m 2 /s for milled and 0.85 × 10 −12 m 2 /s for printed materials were obtained.

recommendations: Do not use the Formlabs 24 h cube figures for design of a swelling layer. For Flexible 80A V2 use the D471 slab data (+8 % and +9 % mass; +3 % and +7 % volume) as the planning basis and measure the real linear strain on your own coupons.

Print one coupon set (Flexible 80A V2, Elastic 50A V2, Rigid 10K, Grey V5; strips 40 x 10 x 0.4, 0.8, 1.6 mm) on the Form 4 and record dry mass, length by calibrated imaging, then mass and length after 1 h, 1 d, 1 wk in water and at 30, 50, 80 %RH in a salt-solution chamber. This gives the missing strain-per-mass coefficient and diffusivity directly and settles the V1 versus V2 and cube versus slab disagreement.
Treat the Denture Base OP sorption disagreement (17.86 at 48 h vs 7.53 at 7 d) as unresolved; if a Formlabs resin is used for a claim, quote the range, not one value.
Report all water uptake with density and thickness; ug/mm3 values convert to mass percent only with a density, which most dental papers omit (I assumed 1.20 g/cm3 for conversions).
Ask Formlabs support whether the 'Flexible 80A Resin' row on the solvent page is V1 and whether D471 water data exist for Elastic 50A V2 / Flexible 50A; I could not find either answer.
